items.title: Migrating from Amazon Q Developer (Where each feature you use lives in Kiro) | Kiro: Zero to Hero 14
items.summary: Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on April 30, 2027. Q Developer in the AWS console and in chat apps is not part of this. This handout shows where each feature you use goes in Kiro, and how to move from VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Visual Studio and Eclipse, and Q Developer CLI, as well as from Q Developer Pro subscriptions. It also includes a table of CLI setting paths, the steps for admins and for each developer, and a suggested phased plan that starts with one pilot team. Based on the kiro.dev docs and the AWS end-of-support announcement, as of November 2026 (Kiro IDE 1.4, Kiro CLI 3.1). This is deck 14, in the Roll it out part of the Kiro: Zero to Hero series.

items.title: Bringing Kiro to your company (Sign-in, models, credits, data, and networking) | Kiro: Zero to Hero 13
items.summary: A handout for administrators on the five things to decide before you bring Kiro to your company (sign-in, models and tools, credits, data, and networking) and where to configure each. It covers IAM Identity Center, Okta, and Microsoft Entra ID, managed-settings.json, credit pooling and usage limits, where data is stored, proxies and PrivateLink, managing updates, and the limits of these controls. The appendix includes a fill-in decision checklist and offboarding steps. Based on the public kiro.dev docs as of November 2026 (Kiro IDE 1.4, Kiro CLI 3.1). This is deck 13, in the Roll it out part of the Kiro: Zero to Hero series.

items.title: Intro to Kiro Web (From sign-in to asking, PRs, and cloud rules) | Kiro: Zero to Hero 04
items.summary: A handout for developers who want to hand off work to Kiro from a browser. You describe a task in Kiro Web, Kiro works on your repo in a cloud sandbox, and you get the result back as a pull request. The deck covers signing in (a personal account needs a Pro plan or higher), connecting GitHub and GitLab, the three ways to work (default mode, Spec mode, and Autonomous mode), starting a task from an issue, the sandbox and its network access settings, Secrets and IAM roles, Configuration Sync, scheduled tasks, and following sessions from your phone (the iOS app is in preview). The running example is a meeting-room booking app. Based on the kiro.dev docs and screenshots of Kiro Web as of November 2026. This is deck 04, in the Get started part of the Kiro: Zero to Hero series.
